subject: Lift-and-shift migration credit request — VP/CFO signoff needed
messages:
From: Nadia Brooks <nadia.brooks@acmehealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Migration credit for Lift & Shift

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the migration tooling. We're preparing an LOI to move a subset of inference traffic off our incumbent and on to Redwood for an initial 6-month ramp (pilot starts May 1).

One ask from procurement: a one-time "lift-and-shift" credit to cover transition costs and the first-month overage risk while we normalize traffic. They'd like something in the 30–40% equivalent on first-month committed consumption, or a $40k onboarding credit.

Can you confirm if Redwood can accommodate a one-time concession like this under a pilot LOI? If so, we'll include the language and route to our legal.

--
Nadia Brooks
Head of Platform Integrations
Acme Health
attachments: acme-pilot-scope.pdf (pdf)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: Migration credit for Lift & Shift — need guidance / VP signoff

Team — forwarding Acme's request. Key facts:
- Pilot ARR (expected) ~ $120k over 6 months; first-month consumption estimate $45k.
- Strategic: incumbent migration makes this a high-signal logo; product-led upstream potential (embedding + Dedicated later).
- Procurement asking for either 35% first-month equivalent discount OR $40k onboarding credit.

I'm okay approving up to a 20% one-time concession from seller-authority for pilot deals, but 35% / $40k needs escalation. Can you weigh commercial impact vs. win probability and advise recommended signoff?

Requested by Nadia — LOI draft will land if we agree to concession language this afternoon. Deadline for LOI inclusion: EOD.

Thanks — Mateo
Sr. Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Migration credit for Lift & Shift — recommendation

Circling back quickly with my recommendation: approve a one-time concession structured as a capped onboarding credit rather than a straight percentage discount. Rationale:

- Preserves list pricing for ongoing consumption (easier to remarket after pilot).
- Limits downside exposure (set credit ceiling).
- Signals partnership value to Acme without creating a durable comp that other accounts will expect.

Proposed structure (recommended):
- $30k onboarding credit applied against first two months (non-transferable).
- Requires 12-month downstream commitment (minimum billed consumption = $240k ARR equivalent) or automatic clawback of unused credit over 12 months.
- Signed LOI with acceptance of Redwood's standard pilot terms.

Financial impact: ~25% equivalent on first-month consumption but capped at $30k. Based on forecast, NPV impact is manageable and justifiable given a >60% chance to convert to paid dedicated work in 12 months.

If Finance (Marissa) agrees, I'll approve and Mateo can confirm with Nadia; if not, escalate to VP/CFO for ad-hoc exception.

--
Jonas Weber
Director, Enterprise Sales

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Migration credit for Lift & Shift — finance input

Thanks Jonas — sensible approach. A few notes before I can greenlight:

1) Please attach the forecasted usage cadence and the pilot SOW assumptions (I need line items that justify $30k cap).
2) Credit treatment: we want the credit to be applied as an invoice credit (not a percentage on list) with explicit clawback if the 12-month minimum isn't met.
3) Approvers: this exceeds Mateo's seller authority and requires VP (me) signoff plus CFO acknowledgement for audit/tax memo. I can sign today if legal confirms LOI language enforces the clawback and the HubSpot deal is updated with the credit line item.

I've attached a quick impact model (discount_impact_model.xlsx) with P&L sensitivity. Please review and send LOI draft to Legal. If we need more than $30k or remove the clawback, escalate to CFO.

--
Marissa Cole
VP, Finance and Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: discount_impact_model.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 31 Mar 2028 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Migration credit for Lift & Shift — finalized terms

Nadia — appreciate the quick turn. Acme, happy to confirm Redwood can include a one-time onboarding credit. Final terms below:

- One-time onboarding credit: $30,000 applied as invoice credit across first two months of pilot consumption.
- Condition: 12-month minimum consumption commitment documented in LOI; unused credit subject to prorated clawback over the 12-month period.
- Credit is non-transferable and applies only to the pilot account outlined in the LOI.
- Redwood legal will add a paragraph to the LOI defining clawback mechanics; Acme should review and confirm acceptance.

Next steps for Acme: confirm acceptance of these terms and return a redlined LOI to contracts@redwood.com. We'll circulate for VP (Marissa) signoff and CFO acknowledgment; Jonas and I will track conversion milestones in HubSpot (deal ACM-2028-003).

If Acme requires the full $40k or a straight 35% discount instead of the credit, we will need explicit CFO approval. Here's the LOI placeholder and the HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACM-2028-003

Look forward to getting this moving.

--
